name: Holiday Apartment "Modern Vienna"
description:
Modern ambiance in a turn of the century house: newly refurbished, lucid existing old dwelling (2nd floor with elevator) in quiet lane.

Bakerys, Viennese wine taverns (“Heurige“) within walking distance.

Just a few minutes to Wilhelminenberg and its castle (with restaurant/café and a great view), to recreation area
Steinhofgründe and Kuffner Sternwarte (historical observatory).
Various public means of transport within walking distance (underground, rapid train, 3 tram lines, buses).

Chef Alberto from Tuscany offers a daily varying menu based on fresh and seasonal products, starting with a range of bruschette, followed by various antipasti, a choice of pasta, a main course of meat and a dessert. The full menu costs €35, if you leave out some courses you will pay accordingly less.

- Taste of India: Indian restaurant on the opposite side of the street: Tasty Indian dishes, reasonably priced.

- Zweitbester, Heumühlgasse 2 (around the corner): Young and modern restaurant, very good food (vegeterian as well as meat and fish), creative recipes, excellent burgers, sunday brunch, in teh evenings occasionaly dj-music.

Also the Donauinsel which is good for rollerskating, picnics, BBQs, jogging and walking (even in the winter its nice and if its a really cold winter you can go ice skating on the Old Donau!) is also a 5 minutes walk from the apartment in the other direction to Augarten.

The apartment is located in the heart of the 20th district in the neighbourhood Brigittenau (originally Donauau), which is considered as a new trend district in Vienna. The name Brigittenau owes the area of the 1645 erected Brigittakapelle and belonged to the 2nd district of Leopoldau from 1850, until it became part of the 20th district around 1900.

In the inner Brigittenau around the Augarten and the Wallensteinplatz, there are several Gründerzeit houses, which have been renovated in recent years. They have been crowned with attic extensions and well-situated young families with children moved into these buildings.

It is the mixture of partly very representative residential housing and the quite urban vivacity of a district center, which makes this neighbourhood so worth living. In addition, everything for the everyday needs such as e.g. the famous Hanover market are in close proximity. The transport connection is excellent.

neighborhood_overview: Leopoldstadt is the 2nd District of Vienna, separated from the city by the Danube Canal. Trendy beach bars and quirky cafes line the canal, making it an ever-popular hangout in the summer months. Leopoldstadt is also known for its large Karmelitermarkt kosher food stalls, which are the traditional hub of the hip Jewish culinary scene in the area. Its abundant offerings draw crowds each year, flocking to this unique and eclectic space. The area is also well known for the iconic Riesenrad Ferris Wheel, which overlooks the Wurstelprater amusement park. Though less opulent than its 1st District counterpart, Leopoldstadt is hailed for its walkable vibe and surrounding green spaces.

The area is also well known for the iconic Riesenrad Ferris Wheel, which overlooks the Wurstelprater amusement park. Though less opulent than its 1st District counterpart, Leopoldstadt is hailed for its walkable vibe and surrounding green spaces.

- **Cultural Landmarks:** Alsergrund is home to several notable sites, including the **Sigmund Freud Museum**, located in Freud's former residence, and the **Josephinum**, which houses an impressive collection of medical history.

- **Architectural Highlights:** The district boasts a variety of architectural styles, from Baroque churches like the **Servitenkirche** to the modernist design of the **Spittelau incineration plant**, redesigned by artist Friedensreich Hundertwasser.

- **Green Spaces:** Guests can enjoy leisurely strolls in nearby parks such as the **Liechtenstein Park**, offering a peaceful retreat amidst the city.

name: Apartment in the green hills of Vienna
description:
The apartment is on the outskirts of Vienna in the old village of Ober. St. Veit. You can go for a walk or run in the Lainzer Tiergarten, go mountain biking in the Wienerwald or eat ice cream in front of the church in Ober St. Veit.

Still, you can quickly get to the center, the next subway and S-Bahn station can be reached in just a few minutes on foot.

To Schönbrunn it takes 15 minutes - on foot it's a wonderful walk through the Hietzinger villa district, although it takes a little longer.
neighborhood_overview:
The neighborhood is a former winemaker town that was incorporated into the city of Vienna over 100 years ago. In addition to small Biedermeier houses, there are the residential buildings typical of Vienna from the Gründerzeit. The center of the Grätzel is the church square of Ober St. Veit. Here you can eat dinner in the evening or get an ice cream (Anton - a must) in the afternoon.

There are of course also supermarkets and shops in the area, within a 5-minute walk you can reach everything you need (supermarkets, bakery, drugstore, pharmacy).

In the immediate vicinity of the property is the Kutschkermarkt. This market is Vienna's last remaining street market next to the fountain market. The likeable market is especially worth a visit on Saturdays. In addition to the fixed market stalls, there are also farmers from the area who sell their regional products – often in organic quality. The offer at the Kutschkermarkt is very high-quality and diverse. There are fruits, vegetables, bread, fish, cheese, wine, juices and jams. In between, flower shops provide a colorful market image.
Opposite the house is the AKH Hospital, and about 100 meters away is the subway station. You can walk to St. Stephen's Cathedral in about 20 minutes.
The 18th district is a modern, bourgeois district where you can eat and live well.

Innere Stadt, Vienna's 1st district, is the historical and cultural heart of the city. This UNESCO World Heritage site exudes imperial charm, with landmarks like St. Stephen’s Cathedral towering as a Gothic masterpiece. The Hofburg Palace speaks of royal splendor, while the State Opera House offers world-class performances. Stroll along the Graben and Kärntner Straße for luxury shopping, or take in the art at the Albertina and Kunsthistorisches Museum. The district's narrow, cobblestone streets are lined with elegant cafés, where you can savor a slice of Sachertorte or sip a classic Wiener Melange.

The district is exceptionally well-connected: trams, buses, and subway lines make it easy to explore Vienna and beyond. Here’s an overview of nearby transportation:

Trams: 1, D, 71
Subway: U1,U3 (Stephansplatz)
Buses: 1A, 2A, 3A
